decision.explanation: The first three terms are 1+6x+15x^2. Setting x=-0.1 gives an approximation of 0.55. The exact value is 0.9^6=0.531441, so the percentage error is |0.55-0.531441|/0.531441 × 100 ≈ 3.49%.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(0.9)^{6}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{6}$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to two decimal places.
after.worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{1}{2!}n(n-1){x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{6} & =1+6x+\frac{1}{2!}\cdot 6\cdot 5\cdot {x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n} \\  & =1+6x+15{x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(1+x)}^{6}≈1+6x+15{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $x=-0.1$ into the above approximation of $(1+x)^{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0.9)^{6} & =(1+(-0.1))^{6} \\  & ≈1+6(-0.1)+15(-0.1)^{2} \\  & =1-6(0.1)+15(0.01) \\  & =1-0.6+0.15 \\  & =0.55\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(0.9)^{6}-0.55|}{(0.9)^{6}}\times 100 \\  & ≈3.49%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

Question 2

Use the first three terms of the binomial expansion of (3+x)5 in ascending powers of x to approximate (2.96)5. Give your answer to three decimal places.

a
227.234
b
227.230
c
227.226
d
227.228
e
227.232
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The binomial theorem for positive integer n states that

(a+b)n=(n0)anb0+(n1)an−1b1+(n2)an−2b2+…+(nn)a0bn.

By substituting a=3, b=x, and n=5, we obtain

(3+x)5=(50)(3)5(x)0+(51)(3)5−1(x)1+(52)(3)5−2(x)2+⋯=1(3)5+5(3)4(x)1+10(3)3(x)2+⋯=243+5(81)(x)+10(27)(x2)+⋯=243+405x+270x2+⋯.

So, for small x, we have

(3+x)5≈243+405x+270x2.

Finally, we substitute x=−0.04 into the above approximation of (3+x)5:

(2.96)5=(3+(−0.04))5≈243+405(−0.04)+270(−0.04)2=243−405(0.04)+270(0.0016)=243−16.2+0.432=227.232,

to three decimal places.

Use the first three terms of the binomial expansion of (2+x)8 in ascending powers of x to approximate (1.87)8. Give your answer to two decimal places.

a
 149.53
b
 151.13
c
 153.16
d
 152.23
e
 150.45
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The binomial theorem for positive integer n states that

(a+b)n=(n0)anb0+(n1)an−1b1+(n2)an−2b2+…+(nn)a0bn.

By substituting a=2, b=x, and n=8, we obtain

(2+x)8=(80)(2)8(x)0+(81)(2)8−1(x)1+(82)(2)8−2(x)2+⋯=1(2)8+8(2)7(x)1+28(2)6(x)2+⋯=256+8(128)(x)+28(64)(x2)+⋯=256+1024x+1792x2+⋯.

So, for small x, we have

(2+x)8≈256+1024x+1792x2.

Finally, we substitute x=−0.13 into the above approximation of (2+x)8:

(1.87)8=(2+(−0.13))8≈256+1024(−0.13)+1792(−0.13)2=256−1024(0.13)+1792(0.0169)=256−133.12+30.2848=153.16,

to two decimal places.

Question 5

Use the first three terms of the binomial expansion of (1+x)10 in ascending powers of x to approximate (0.999)10. Give your answer to six decimal places.

a
0.999950
b
0.990043
c
0.009955
d
1.010045
e
0.990045
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that when n is a positive integer,

(1+x)n=1+nx+12!n(n−1)x2+⋯+xn.

Therefore,

(1+x)10=1+10x+12⋅10⋅9⋅x2+⋯+x10=1+10x+45x2+⋯+x10.

So, for small x, we have

(1+x)10≈1+10x+45x2.

Finally, we substitute x=−0.001 into the above approximation of (1+x)10:

(0.999)10=(1+(−0.001))10≈1+10(−0.001)+45(−0.001)2=1−10(0.001)+45(0.000001)=1−0.01+0.000045=0.990045,

to six decimal places.
